context: Start with a w0 revalidation against current origin/develop and the merged PR heads; record exact source lines and the current adapter behavior before editing. Define one canonical matrix for SQL and DataFrame options, including aliases such as -df, and classify options as execution-only, transport/security-sensitive, or resource-consuming. Add table-driven tests that exercise validation, normal synchronous execution, durable-job persistence/retry, and effective adapter application. Prefer an adapter-facing inspection or applied-setting receipt over a mock that only observes kwargs. Make any new option require an explicit consumer contract, bounded values, redaction review, and a negative test for rejection or unsafe combinations. Document rejected alternatives such as copying the CLI registry wholesale or relying on forwarding-only mocks.
description: Create the shared contract guard for the MCP platform_options surface before fixing individual adapters. The adversarial review of PR #1465 found that the manually maintained allowlist accepts values that are ignored, dropped, or misrouted by the real adapters (DuckDB threads, Databricks clustering fields, Velox docker, and Modin pandas), while the ClickHouse and Dask entries create security/resource-envelope risk. Revalidate those findings against the current origin/develop tree and build a table-driven contract matrix mapping every accepted key to its consumer, effective runtime field, security class, bounded resource envelope, and required test. The matrix must fail closed when an allowlisted key has no effective consumer or when a consumer contract drifts. This is a prerequisite for all adapter-specific remediation and must not widen the MCP surface merely to make tests pass.

anti_patterns.dont: Copy the full CLI platform-option registry into MCP
anti_patterns.instead: Add an option only when its consumer, security classification, bound, and negative test are recorded in the matrix.
anti_patterns.why: The CLI contains credentials, endpoints, paths, installation controls, and unbounded resource knobs that violate the remote MCP boundary.

anti_patterns.dont: Treat forwarding to a mocked adapter as proof that an option works
anti_patterns.instead: Assert the effective adapter field or applied runtime setting and cover the durable worker path separately.
anti_patterns.why: The review already found a green forwarding test for DuckDB threads even though the real adapter ignores that key.

anti_patterns.dont: Use a passing current-tree command as the only verification
anti_patterns.instead: Include at least one rung whose expected text states that it exits non-zero on the unfixed tree and add regression evidence for the fixed behavior.
anti_patterns.why: A green pre-fix test can verify nothing about the defect being fixed.

preserves.behavior: Durable jobs persist only normalized, non-secret options and replay the same validated object after retries or worker restarts.
Existing stdio and sessionless Streamable HTTP tool schemas and error codes remain compatible except where a documented unsafe option is intentionally rejected.
No test starts a real cloud service, contacts a user-configured endpoint, or stores credentials in source, fixtures, logs, or evidence.
The MCP allowlist remains narrower than the CLI option registry and never accepts credentials, hosts, DSNs, filesystem paths, package installation controls, or driver version controls.
